title: QuasarConvexHessianLipschitz.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Quasar convexity permits nonconvex objectives; convexity is not required.

problem_class.label: quasar
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization with a global minimizer x⋆ satisfying γ(f(x)−f(x⋆)) ≤ ⟨∇f(x),x−x⋆⟩ for every x, where 0<γ≤1.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: The joint oracle returns ∇f(x) exactly for every history and seed; there is no oracle error or dependence affecting replies.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Each query at x returns the exact value f(x), together with its gradient and Hessian, in one joint oracle call.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact full Hessian oracle: the joint reply includes D(∇f)(x) as a continuous linear operator.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: f is C² with globally H-Lipschitz Hessian in operator norm, H>0, and ‖∇²f(x₀)‖≤L₀ with L₀≥0. A hidden minimizer x⋆ satisfies ‖x₀−x⋆‖≤R, R>0. E, x₀, H, γ, R, L₀ and ε>0 are public; no global gradient Lipschitz constant or bounded level set is assumed.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a point x with f(x)−f(x⋆)≤ε for a global minimizer x⋆.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee holds almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, with a fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: A meaningful quasar-convex variant using Hessian Lipschitz continuity and an initial Hessian bound, without global gradient smoothness or bounded level sets.

descriptionHtml:
Quasar-Convex Minimization with Lipschitz Hessian

We consider minimizing a twice continuously differentiable function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. For γ∈(0,1], the function is γ-quasar-convex relative to a global minimizer x⋆, with ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R for a given starting point x0∈E and radius R>0. Its Hessian is H-Lipschitz, where H>0, and has operator norm at most L0≥0 at x0. The oracle returns f(x), ∇f(x), and ∇2f(x) at x. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm. The Hessian ∇2f(x):E→E is the derivative of the gradient at x. The algorithm receives E, x0, H, γ, R, L0, and ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Hessian regularity). The function f is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable on E, and ∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤H∥x−y∥for all x,y∈E,∥∇2f(x0)∥op≤L0.

Assumption 2 (Quasar convexity and initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that, for every x∈E, f(x⋆)≤f(x),γ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤⟨∇f(x),x−x⋆⟩, and ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Queries may be made at any point of E, and each oracle reply is the exact triple (f(x),∇f(x),∇2f(x)). After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s. Here x⋆ is a fixed global minimizer; all global minimizers have the same objective value.

comparisonHtml:
On a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, f∈C2 has H-Lipschitz Hessian and a global minimizer x⋆ satisfying γ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤⟨∇f(x),x−x⋆⟩ for every x. Assume H,R,ε>0, 0<γ≤1, ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, and ∥∇2f(x0)∥≤L0 with L0≥0. Exact queries return (f,∇f,∇2f). Result (1) uses known H,γ,R,L0,ε and constructs an accelerated cubic Newton output x^ with deterministic accuracy f(x^)−f(x⋆)≤ε; the setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

Comparison for QuasarConvexHessianLipschitz.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) QuasarAcceleratedCubicNewton (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O((1+γ−3/2T3/8)ℓ) triple calls, including coupling-search queries.
(2) Cubic Newton (Nesterov and Polyak 2006), Thm. 4 O(1+(HD3/ε)1/2) triple calls. Star-convex (γ=1); bounded convex neighborhood of the initial sublevel set, diameter D. (1): for D≍R, T3/8ℓ instead of T1/2 as T→∞. Scope: removes bounded-sublevel-set requirement and allows γ<1. (1) needs γ,L0 and a fixed horizon; much worse constants. Reported crossover only around T≳1037 for γ=1,D=R.
(3) (Hinder et al. 2020), Thm. 2 O((1+γ−1RL/ε)ℓL) function/gradient calls, including search. Special case: globally L-smooth. (1) removes global L-smoothness. On the overlap, fewer raw calls for sufficiently small ε (crossover ε≈γ4L4/(H3R), ignoring logarithms); different oracle costs. (1) requires Hessians and H; leading γ−3/2 instead of γ−1.
(4) (Lee and Valiant 2016), Thm. 2.5 O(poly(n,δ−1,log+⁡(1/ε),log+⁡(1/F),log+⁡R,log+⁡B)) weak sampling value calls. Star-convex; |f|≤B within 10nR of x0. Returns a Gaussian with (1−δ) good mass, with probability 1−F. (1): dimension-free cost; deterministic point accuracy instead of a randomized Gaussian-region guarantee; also covers γ<1. Rates and outputs are not directly comparable. (1) needs smoothness and Hessians; polynomial rather than polylogarithmic accuracy dependence at fixed dimension.
(5) Accelerated cubic Newton (Nesterov 2005), Thm. 2 O(1+T1/3) triple calls. Special case: convex (γ=1); cited 2005 preprint. (1) extends scope from convexity to γ-quasar-convexity. (1) is slower on the convex overlap: T3/8ℓ instead of T1/3 for T≫1.

Abbr: T=HR3/ε; ℓ=log⁡(2+T+L0/(HR)+γ−1); ℓL=1+log⁡(1+γ−1RL/ε); log+⁡a=1+max{0,log⁡a}. D is the neighborhood diameter in (2); L is the global gradient Lipschitz constant in (3); n=dim⁡E, δ,F∈(0,1) are mass-error and failure tolerances, and B>0 is the local absolute-value bound in (4). Triple calls return (f,∇f,∇2f); weak sampling value calls evaluate at Gaussian-sampled points. poly denotes an unspecified fixed polynomial.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension
import Mathlib.Order.Filter.Extr

namespace LongTails.Setups.QuasarConvexHessianLipschitz

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  x0 : E
  H : ℝ
  γ : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  L₀ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE

def QuasarConvexAt {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] (f : E → ℝ) (γ : ℝ) (xstar : E) : Prop :=
  IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ∀ x, γ * (f x - f xstar) ≤ ⟪gradient f x, x - xstar⟫

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := ℝ × p.E × (p.E →L[ℝ] p.E)
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.H ∧ 0 < p.γ ∧ p.γ ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 ≤ p.L₀ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    ContDiff ℝ 2 f ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) y‖ ≤ p.H * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) p.x0‖ ≤ p.L₀ ∧
    (∃ xstar, QuasarConvexAt f p.γ xstar ∧ ‖p.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ p.R) ∧
    (∀ k x seed, O.answer k (0, x) seed = (f x, gradient f x, fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x))
  successful p f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.QuasarConvexHessianLipschitz
